findings.title: Factory sender-selection in AuthFeatureConfiguration has no automated test
findings.detail: Both planned unit tests construct DevConsoleSmsSender directly with env stubs; neither exercises the AuthFeatureConfiguration factory (Sms:DevLogCode=true -> DevConsoleSmsSender, false -> ConsoleSmsSender). AC#1 (dev selects the code-logging sender) and AC#3 (masked ConsoleSmsSender is the default when the flag is unset) are therefore only manually verified. The customer-auth regression tests override ISmsSender in ConfigureTestServices, so they bypass the factory entirely. The security-critical branch (runtime env guard) IS pinned by the Production-masks test, and the selection is a 3-line config read mirroring the untested Seed:Enabled precedent — hence MEDIUM, not a blocker.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally add a focused DI test: build a ServiceCollection, run AuthFeatureConfiguration.AddFeatureDependencies with Sms:DevLogCode=true then false, resolve ISmsSender, and assert the concrete type (DevConsoleSmsSender vs ConsoleSmsSender). Accept as-is if matching the Seed:Enabled precedent, but note the coverage gap in the WI handoff.

findings.title: Dev branch logs the raw unmasked phone number (PII), beyond the documented exception
findings.detail: The planned dev template `logger.LogInformation("Dev SMS {Phone} {Body}", phone, message)` passes the full E.164 phone unmasked. The spec's documented exception to rules/logging.md authorizes logging the OTP code/body only — it does not mention the phone number. The masked branch (and existing ConsoleSmsSender) log only last-4. This is an additional, unstated PII deviation. Dev-only, so LOW.
findings.suggested_fix: Either mask the phone in the dev branch too (reuse the last-4 helper, keeping only {Body} raw), or explicitly widen the bold class comment / spec exception to state the dev branch also logs the full phone and why that is acceptable in Development.

findings.title: AuthFeatureConfiguration XML summary becomes stale after the factory change
findings.detail: The existing AddFeatureDependencies summary states ConsoleSmsSender 'is registered unconditionally — no production SMS gateway exists in v1.' After replacing the unconditional AddSingleton with the gated factory, this is false/misleading. It also mislabels the lifetime as 'scoped' while registration is singleton. Won't trip -warnaserror. rules/csharp-style.md#xml-documentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the XML summary to describe the Sms:DevLogCode gate (DevConsoleSmsSender when true, else ConsoleSmsSender), correct 'scoped' to 'singleton', and drop the 'registered unconditionally' claim.
